english.note: This is the all-purpose choice for possession, availability, family relationships, contents, scheduled classes, illnesses, and having children.
Use this as the all-purpose everyday way to say that someone owns or possesses something.
Use this as the all-purpose spoken way to say that a container or item has something in it.
This is the all-purpose colloquial verb for having or owning something.
Use this casual choice when simply listing what a group, set, or invention has in it.
Use 有 for possessing something or for a shop having an item available, rather than for physically carrying it.
Use this all-purpose verb when something has or displays a mark, appearance, name, reputation, or bodily feature.

english.note: Use this everyday verb for saying that something exists or is present in a place, situation, or set of possibilities.
Use this when get means possess something or indicate that something exists in a place or situation.
Use 有 for existence and for measurements expressed as an amount possessed, especially age or duration such as having three hundred years of history.
